Subject: Layered program lead realignment & review process

Team — attaching a short draft for how we can phase the program-lead realignment across Product, Infra, and Platform over the next two quarters. High-level goals: reduce duplicate manager touchpoints, clarify scope for program leads (execution vs. roadmap), and preserve continuity for customer-facing owners.

Quick context: this came out of the last leadership sync where we saw ~25% overlap in PM/Program responsibilities across three teams and a recurring question about escalation ownership. Oliver helped model two phasing options (conservative / accelerated).

Requested: please review the attached phase plan (realignment_phases.pdf) and the proposed role matrix (role_scopes_v1.xlsx). I want to lock a timeline and a comms approach by EOD Monday so we can align with total rewards and the Q3 comp calendar.

Major open questions in the doc:
- Which program leads should remain dotted-line to product vs. move to direct reports for speed of execution
- Proposed handoff owners for ongoing customer escalations
- Candidate pilot team for the accelerated path (if we choose to pilot)

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick read + inline comments in the doc (preferably in Google Doc linked below) by Monday 12pm PT
2) 60m sync Tues to decide pilot vs. conservative path
3) HR checkpoint (Mina) for comms and comp implications before any one-on-ones

Links: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XyZ-example-realignment-plan
JIRA: ORG-1423

Attachments: realignment_phases.pdf; role_scopes_v1.xlsx

Thanks — Priya

Thanks Priya — important doc. A few concerns from Product leadership perspective:

- Performance review alignment: Q3 calibration is the week after the proposed pilot start. If we change reporting lines before calibration there will be noise in ratings and bonus allocation. We need an HR gating item to ensure managers are calibrated on any new reporting before comp decisions are finalized.

- Sensitive cases: there are a handful of program leads on performance plans; moving them under new managers mid-review will trigger appeals and fairness questions. We should identify these individuals now and exclude them from the first wave.

- Customer continuity: suggest a mandatory overlap window (two sprints) where old and new leads are both accountable. That reduces support tickets and preserves SLAs.

Can Mina confirm the recommended minimum time between reporting change and comp calibration? Also, happy to run the pilot on Observability infra if Vivek wants a less customer-facing starting point.

Laura

Subject: Re: Layered program lead realignment & review process — HR checkpoints and comms guidance

Folks — thanks for the heads-up. A few practical rules from People & Ops so we don't create unintended fairness or legal exposure:

1) Comp calibration rule: changes to manager assignment should be finalized no later than 30 days before the start of formal compensation calibration meetings. If we must change closer than 30 days, we need explicit documented rationale and a calibration addendum signed by both managers.

2) Performance plan exceptions: anyone currently on a PIP or formal improvement plan should be excluded from reassignment during the active plan period. HR will compile and share the list by Monday noon.

3) Comms: central comms must be staged — a leadership announcement, followed by manager-level talking points, then one-on-one scripts. I attached the updated comms policy (comm_policy_v2.docx) that includes a redaction checklist and guidance on timing with external customers.

4) Confidentiality: keep lists of impacted individuals restricted to People & direct execs until at-risk comms are ready. Do not include tenure or compensation numbers in shared docs.

I will also coordinate with Total Rewards on any comp-side implications once the pilot decision is made.

— Mina
Mina Haddad | Head, People Ops & Compliance | Redwood Inference
